question: A hot-air balloon directly above point A is rising vertically at 2 m/s. An observer at point B, 500 m due east of A, watches the balloon. At the moment when the angle of elevation is 30°, how long until it reaches an angle of elevation of 60°? (Assume no horizontal drift.)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Distance covered = Base × (tan θ₂ − tan θ₁)

Vertical Distance = 500 × (tan 60° − tan 30°) = 500 × (√3 − 1/√3)

Vertical Distance = 500 × (2/√3) = 1000/√3 m

Time = Distance / Speed = (1000/√3) / 2 = 500/√3 s

Time ≈ 500 / 1.73205 = 288.675 s

**∴ The correct option is (1).**
